name: Osaka Castle
desc: A gold-trimmed castle on a moat with cherry trees for days. The park is free; the keep is pocket change.

name: Dotonbori
desc: A neon canyon of giant mechanical crabs and the running-man sign. The city's entire personality in one glowing strip.

name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
desc: Osaka's kitchen — grilled scallops, tuna cheeks, and free entry. Your nose does the spending for you.

name: Umeda Sky Building
desc: Twin towers holding a floating rooftop observatory. A night view that makes all that overtime feel almost worth it.

name: Shitennoji Temple
desc: One of Japan's oldest temples — 1,400 years of calm for less than a convenience-store coffee.

name: Shinsekai
desc: A retro neon time-warp thick with kushikatsu smoke. Remember: double-dipping the sauce is the only crime here.

name: Tsutenkaku Tower
desc: The scrappy little Eiffel of the south side. Rub Billiken's feet for luck — you'll need it, dreamer.

name: Sumiyoshi Taisha
desc: An ancient shrine with a drum-arched bridge steep enough to count as a tiny pilgrimage. Free blessings included.

name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
desc: A whale shark doing slow laps around a building-sized tank. Certified date-night cheat code.

name: Universal Studios Japan
desc: Mario and wizards in one park. The splurge square on everyone's someday bingo card.
